front: What is the Put-Call Parity formula for European options (no dividends)?
back: C + K × e^(-rT) = P + S, where C is Call premium, P is Put premium, S is spot price, and K × e^(-rT) is present value of strike.

front: Why must Put-Call Parity hold in efficient markets?
back: A Fiduciary Call (C + PV(K)) and a Protective Put (P + S) generate identical payoffs under all future outcomes. If their costs differed, risk-free arbitrage would occur.
A portfolio condition where the net sum of all Deltas equals zero (∑Δ = 0), insulating portfolio value from small spot price fluctuations.

front: How do you calculate stock shares needed to Delta-hedge a short option position?
back: Required Shares = Total Option Contracts × Lot Size × Option Delta.

front: Why do Delta hedges require dynamic rebalancing over time?
back: Because Gamma causes Delta to change whenever spot prices move. Traders must continuously buy or sell stock to maintain net zero Delta.

front: What happens if Put-Call Parity is violated in the market?
back: A risk-free arbitrage opportunity is created. Arbitrageurs buy the cheaper portfolio and sell the expensive portfolio until parity is restored.
